signals.title: AUD/USD — Geopolitical Risk + Retail Extreme
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7082, reversing recent gains as TIER-1 geopolitical headlines regarding Iran risks lift the US Dollar's safe-haven appeal ahead of FOMC minutes. The pair remains technically supported above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7034/0.6996/0.6945), but commodity selling pressure noted by CME Group research adds a secondary headwind. Speculative positioning via COT LF remains net long (+45,727), while retail sentiment has reached a 82% short extreme. This institutional vs. retail divergence typically suggests a late-trend squeeze environment, though the immediate geopolitical shock is forcing a temporary AUD pullback. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, pending stabilization above SMA20 after the geopolitical flush. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes release later today. Risk: Escalation in the Strait of Hormuz triggers a broad VIX spike above 25, forcing a disorderly unwind of AUD longs.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is holding at 159.43, remaining below its SMA20/50 resistance cluster (160.17/161.07) as intervention risks at the 160.00 handle persist. While a +268bp SOFR-TONA carry differential fundamentally supports the USD bid, the options market is signaling heavy downside protection demand. The 25d Risk Reversal (RR) has reached a strong -1.96 put skew, marking a significant divergence from the carry-positive backdrop. Additionally, the USD/JPY vs VIX correlation has flipped to +0.405 (z=+1.53σ), indicating that JPY's traditional safe-haven function is currently impaired. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, capped by intervention risk at 160.00. Catalyst: BoJ Takaichi headlines and next policy meeting. Risk: A confirmed break above 160.00 without MoF intervention is likely to trigger a fast carry-led squeeze toward 162.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5866, sitting just above its SMA20 (0.5854) and SMA200 (0.5837) support levels. COT LF positioning shows a crowded net short of -34,031, placing it at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=-2.00). This extreme bearish positioning contradicts the improving fundamental data, with the NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) currently at +12.6, indicating a moderate positive bias in realized data. With the RBNZ still in a hiking cycle and a 2.5% policy rate, the disconnect between spec shorts and data outperformance creates an asymmetric short-squeeze risk. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD, targeting an unwind of crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias remains. Risk: A break below the SMA200 at 0.5837 invalidates the technical floor and validates the spec short.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3533, positioned above all major moving averages following a steady 1-month climb of +0.65%. Despite the bullish price action, the options market is pricing in significant uncertainty with an IV of 11.0% against an HV30 of 5.8%, resulting in a substantial +5.2% Vol Risk Premium (VRP). This elevated premium suggests that institutions are paying up for protection rather than chasing the spot move higher. COT data shows LF net longs are becoming crowded at the 90th percentile (z=+1.23), confirming a heavy speculative consensus that may struggle to find new buyers at these levels. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, high hedging costs limit attractive entry for new longs. Catalyst: UK CPI release. Risk: UK CPI beat re-ignites hike pricing, forcing a continuation despite high vol premiums.
